faq: Which tools can it pull numbers from?
Shopify, WooCommerce, Google Analytics, Google Ads, Meta Ads, Stripe, QuickBooks, Mailchimp, Klaviyo and Google Sheets are common. We confirm access for each before you order.
Will the numbers match what I see in each tool?
They should, within the way each tool counts. Tools often count orders or visits differently, so we state the definition for every figure and test against the tool itself.
Can different people get different reports?
Yes, in the Premium package. For instance, a short summary for the owner and a detailed one for the marketing lead, each on its own schedule.
Do I need a special reporting tool?
No. We can build it in Google Sheets or Looker Studio, sent by email as a PDF or link. Any subscription for a paid tool is billed to you, and we advise on the simplest option.

desc:
Weekly report automation sent on schedule pulls your sales, ad spend, orders and sign-ups into one clear message at the same time every week. Ecom Swift LLC connects your tools, builds the report and delivers it to your inbox or Slack.

## What is an automated weekly report?

An automated weekly report is a summary that builds and sends itself. It reads figures from the tools you already use, places them in a set layout, compares them with the previous period and delivers the result on a fixed day. A short note in plain words points out anything unusual, so you do not have to hunt for it in a table.

It replaces the Monday routine of opening several dashboards, copying numbers into a sheet and hoping you did not paste the wrong cell.

## Why manual reporting drifts and gets skipped

A report that takes an hour to compile gets postponed, then dropped when the week is busy. The numbers also change shape: one person counts orders before refunds, another after, and the layout slowly shifts from month to month. After a while nobody trusts the report enough to act on it.

Hand-built reports also hide the decision itself. When the effort goes into collecting the numbers, little energy is left to ask what they mean. Every hour spent pasting is an hour not spent on the question of what to change.

## How regular reports improve decisions

A report that arrives on time creates a habit. When the same figures appear in the same order every week, a change stands out immediately: ad spend rising while orders stay flat, sign-ups dropping after a site edit, or a product suddenly selling faster. You can respond within days rather than discovering the shift at the end of a quarter.

Consistency matters as much as speed. With defined formulas, the figure for "orders" means the same thing every time, so comparisons are fair. Different readers can get different versions, such as a short note for the owner and a detailed view for the marketer, so each person sees only what they need.

## What a great automated report includes

- A short list of key figures chosen because someone acts on them.
- Clear definitions for each figure, written down once.
- Data pulled from each source tool on a schedule.
- Change from the previous week shown beside every figure.
- Charts for the main trends, kept simple.
- A plain-language note on any unusual movement.
- Delivery by email, Slack or both at a fixed time.
- Separate versions for different readers.
- Daily or monthly variants when you need them.
- Your logo and colors on the layout.

## How we build it

We begin by asking which decisions the report should support. From that we agree on a short set of figures, the tool each one comes from and how each is calculated. We connect the sources, build the layout and run the report against past data so you can compare it with what you see in each tool.

Basic connects one source and sends up to a handful of figures by email. Standard combines several sources, adds charts, sends to email and Slack, and includes a note on unusual changes. Premium combines more sources, adds weekly, daily and monthly versions, applies your branding and creates separate versions for different readers. If a number differs from the one in a tool, we explain why, for example a different time zone or a refund timing rule.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Choose figures you would act on if they moved.
- Write down how each figure is calculated.
- Check the first reports against the source tools.
- Pick a delivery time when you will read it.
- Tell us who should get which version.

**Avoid:**
- Filling the report with every number available.
- Mixing time zones or date ranges between sources.
- Changing a definition without noting it.
- Sending the same long report to everyone.
- Treating one unusual week as a trend.

## Who it is for

An online store owner who wants sales, ad spend and orders in one message every Monday. An agency that sends clients a weekly summary and wants to stop assembling it by hand. A manager who needs a short view of sign-ups, support volume and revenue without logging in to four tools.

## What we need from you

Tell us which figures matter, where they live and who should receive the report. Share an example of a report you build by hand, if you have one. Access is given to us as a collaborator, staff or team user, or through read-only connections where the tool allows. We never ask for passwords, and you own the report and its connections.
